title: Cryptography dep bump and public client interface slimming for SDKs
creator: Maya Chen
description: Goal: perform coordinated, low-risk dependency upgrades across Python/JS/Go SDKs to remove known crypto/transport security warnings, reduce vector surface from legacy helper APIs, and provide a clear migration path for customers. This ticket covers: 1) Bump cryptography-related deps (Python 'cryptography' 40.x -> 41.x, 'PyNaCl' 1.5.x -> 1.5.0+compat), Node 'jsonwebtoken' and transport crypto helpers to LTS versions, and Go 'golang.org/x/crypto' to latest patch. 2) Remove/soft-deprecate legacy convenience wrappers that surface raw header manipulation (legacy 'raw_auth' utilities) and unify token header normalization across languages. 3) Add compatibility shims in the client major to allow a 90-day deprecation window and auto-logging of usage of removed methods. 4) CI and release gating: add dependency vulnerability scanner step, runtime smoke tests, and canary rollout plan. Success criteria: upgrade completes without regressions in core integration tests, no new CVEs introduced by dependency bumps, migration guide published, and canary environment serves >1M tokens/day with <1% error delta versus baseline.
comments: 2025-02-11 - Maya Chen: Created initial tech plan after triage. Rationale: several security scanners flagged transient issues in our transitive crypto deps and legacy helper functions increase risk surface for customer token handling. Proposed coordinated cross-SDK bump to avoid staggered minor releases that confuse users.

2025-02-13 - Liam O'Connor: Completed inventory of direct/indirect crypto deps in repositories: python-redwood-client, node-redwood, go-redwood. Noted 12 transitive packages for review. Drafted patch strategy: prefer non-breaking patch/minor upgrades; where necessary introduce thin adapter layer rather than immediate breaking change.
2025-02-14 - Design/Docs request (via Slack): Add clear migration snippet for changed auth helpers; will produce a small code sample per language. Assigned to @Aisha Patel (docs).

2025-02-15 - Engineering note: Decided to standardize on platform-level token header normalization (strip duplicate X-Request-ID, normalize Authorization casing) instead of per-sdk heuristics. Pros: reduces duplicate logic and future drift. Cons: requires minor runtime change; added integration test coverage.

2025-02-16 - Security review kickoff: security team (Raj Singh) requested an explicit audit for OpenSSL-linked transitive packages in Go and Node. Marked security_review_required=true and added additional gating in CI. Pending security audit completion.

2025-02-17 - PRs opened: python PR #412 (https://github.com/redwood-inference/python-redwood-client/pull/412) - bumps 'cryptography' and migrates a single helper to new API; node PR #278 (https://github.com/redwood-inference/node-redwood/pull/278) - replaces deprecated jwt signing helper with 'jose' recommended API; go PR #134 (https://github.com/redwood-inference/go-redwood/pull/134) - updates go.mod and pins 'golang.org/x/crypto' with minimal changes. Early CI failures on python due to older pip resolver; fixed by pinning a compatible 'cffi' patch.

2025-02-18 - Integration smoke run: Canary of node client behind canary proxy (5% traffic) — observed no auth failures; latency 95th increased by 1.8% (within acceptable threshold). Python canary (2% traffic) saw a flaky test related to timestamp parsing in legacy helper; created follow-up sub-issue ENG-842401.

2025-02-19 - Code review feedback: PM requested that we not remove the legacy 'raw_auth' shorthand immediately. Decision: convert it into a deprecation shim that emits a single structured warning and points to migration docs. Added automatic telemetry tag when shim is used to measure usage before removal.

2025-02-20 - Next steps: finalize security audit, merge PRs after green CI + security signoff, publish migration guide with concrete code examples and a snippet for 'how to detect shim usage', schedule a staged rollout (canary 5% -> 25% -> 100% over 7 days) with rollback criteria defined.
